messages:
maria: Heads up — customer 'Greenway' getting 401 invalid_api_key right after creating a Read-only token in the Dashboard. Can repro locally.

alex: Can you paste the curl you used + the exact Authorization header (mask middle if needed)?

maria: Sure. Command I ran: 
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ro-1a2b3c4d5e6f' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{}'
```
Note: when we view the new key in Dashboard it shows as `ro_1a2b3c4d5e6f` (underscore). Copying from the copy button and pasting into my terminal yields `ro-1a2b3c4d5e6f` (hyphen).

sam: That explains the 401 — our token parser expects the read-only prefix to be `ro_` (underscore). `ro-` gets rejected at validation. Can you paste the raw header that you sent (so we see the exact char)?

maria: I pasted it exactly as copied. Server response was: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid"}`

alex: What browser/os are they using? Any console errors? @deploy-bot did we ship anything touching the copy-to-clipboard UI?

maria: MacOS 12.6, Safari 16.3. No console errors visible. Copy button produced the hyphen on paste. On Windows Chrome copying from the same Dashboard entry produces the correct underscore.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled dashboard release 2026.3.4 ~5m ago (includes small clipboard helper tweak staged to fix copy quirks).

sam: Repro'd locally on Safari — copy helper normalizer has a bad regex that replaces underscores with hyphens when the clipboard payload hits a certain sanitizer path. I'll prep a hotfix. For immediate mitigation we can: 1) accept `ro-` server-side as a compatibility shim for ~24h, and 2) push a UI quickfix to stop the substitution.

alex: Please do both. In the meantime tell the customer to manually replace the `-` with `_` in the token string as a workaround. I'll log a critical bug and add postmortem items (unit tests + cross-browser copy checks).

maria: Messaging customer now with the manual-replace workaround and ETA ~1h for hotfix. Apologized. Will update thread after fix deploys.
